info.name: Sitwego Beckn BPP — via mock-BAP harness
info.description:
Drive the full Beckn booking flow from Postman.

Postman cannot Ed25519-sign request bodies or receive asynchronous Beckn callbacks, so every request here goes through the mock-BAP signing harness (`FLOW=serve ... cargo run -p beckn-bpp-adapter --bin mock_bap`). The harness signs the exact bytes with the BAP key, forwards to the real gateway/adapter, and collects the async `on_*` callbacks for polling — signatures stay ON end to end.

Happy path (all requests need NO body edits):
1. `search` → poll `callbacks (all)` until `on_search` arrives
2. `select` → `on_select` (quote)
3. `init` → `on_init` (order id, harvested into the session automatically)
4. `confirm` → `on_confirm`, then keep polling: the unsolicited `on_status` RIDE_ASSIGNED arrives once a driver accepts (use scratchpad `driver_sim.py` for a simulated driver)
5. `status` / `track` / `cancel` — empty bodies, order id comes from the session

`GET session` shows what the harness has learned (transaction id, bpp, catalog item, order id). Any request accepts `{"message": …}` to override the default body.

request.description:
Signed search via the gateway `/bg/search`. Opens a fresh transaction (resets the harness session). Default intent uses PICKUP_GPS/DROPOFF_GPS from the harness env; override with a raw JSON body like:

{"message": {"intent": {"fulfillment": {"stops": [{"type": "START", "location": {"gps": "-1.2864, 36.8172"}}, {"type": "END", "location": {"gps": "-1.3192, 36.9258"}}]}}}}
Signed select, direct to the BPP. Default body selects the first catalog item from the last on_search. Fails with a clear error if the catalog was empty (no driver online).
Signed init. The on_init callback carries the durable order id; the harness harvests it into the session automatically.

Signed confirm — enters REAL dispatch on the api service. Default body uses the session order id and CUSTOMER_NAME/CUSTOMER_PHONE from the harness env. After on_confirm, keep polling callbacks: the unsolicited on_status RIDE_ASSIGNED arrives when a driver accepts (run scratchpad driver_sim.py to simulate one).
Signed status for the session's order id. Reply arrives as an on_status callback.
Signed track. The on_track callback carries the tracking URL (never raw GPS).
Signed cancel for the session's order id. Expect an on_cancel callback with cancelled_by=CONSUMER. Refused (error callback) once the ride is in progress — v1 policy.
Every on_* callback received so far, oldest first. Poll this after each action — Beckn replies are asynchronous.
Filter by action: on_search / on_select / on_init / on_confirm / on_status / on_cancel / on_track.
What the harness has learned from callbacks: transaction_id, bpp_id/bpp_uri, provider/item from the catalog, order_id. This is what fills the empty-body defaults.
Empty the stored callback list (the session is untouched; a new search resets that).
